subject.title: Feature request: first-class .env / environment-backed secret config UX

question: What SecretRef metadata may Control UI expose for env-backed secrets, and should env variable names or resolved/unresolved state be shown by default?
rationale: The requested UX improves secret hygiene, but showing env names, provider aliases, or resolution state can disclose operator setup details, so automation should not choose that boundary alone.

options.title: Conservative source-aware UI
options.body: Show masked source labels and safe resolved/unresolved state, reveal env variable names only where maintainers approve, and keep writes aligned with existing SecretRef configure/apply paths.

options.title: Minimal read-only badge
options.body: Replace the generic structured placeholder with a safe `SecretRef configured` indicator while leaving editing in Raw/CLI until a fuller design is approved.

options.title: Defer UI disclosure
options.body: Keep current Control UI behavior and improve docs/CLI guidance only, avoiding new metadata exposure until security review defines policy.

recommendation.title: Conservative source-aware UI
recommendation.body: Show masked source labels and safe resolved/unresolved state, reveal env variable names only where maintainers approve, and keep writes aligned with existing SecretRef configure/apply paths.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest merged history on the SecretRef contract and Control UI/RPC round-trip behavior that should anchor the disclosure decision.
